_note: composition_motif_adopt asked with a NAMED system motif. See the scenario's _why_this_prompt.

scenarios.prompt: Adopt motif — copy the built-in trope 'Face-Slap Reversal' into my library so I can customise it.
scenarios.prompt_source: meta.synonyms['adopt motif'] + ['copy trope to my library'], verbatim.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM motif WHERE status='active' AND owner_user_id IS NULL
seed_assert.why:
EIGHTY-FOUR system/unlisted motifs already exist, so there is genuinely something to adopt and the model must FIND one — composition_motif_book_list / a motif search is the supplier. Read from the store rather than assumed. NOTE the deliberate asymmetry with batch 15's arc templates: the system arc-template library is EMPTY, so this is the first tool in the loop whose cross-tenancy source actually has rows.

🔴 status='active' ADDED 2026-08-23 by the lifecycle-predicate gate. The tool reads active rows only (get_by_codes filters status='active'), so without this the assertion could pass over rows the tool is structurally unable to see — which is exactly what happened to composition_motif_link_edit for fifteen runs. Verified NOT to change the seeded value: all 84 system motifs are active today, so this tightens the assertion without moving its number.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM motif WHERE owner_user_id='019d5e3c-7cc5-7e6a-8b27-1344e148bf7c' AND code LIKE 'adopted-%'
seed_assert.why: SCOPED, not a headcount of the caller's library. That library is 152 and MOVING — the other scenarios in this batch seed into it, and my own seed-smoke added a row while I was verifying the fixture. The system side (84, owner_user_id NULL) is stable and is asserted above; here the check is simply that no ADOPTED clone exists yet, so one appearing is attributable to this turn.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: a clone lands with NO confirm card (Tier W — its own description says adopting 'crosses the tenancy boundary and counts against your library quota', which is why it is human-confirmed), OR the model invents a motif_id rather than listing the built-ins first, OR it passes retag_genres the author never mentioned — retagging is optional and silently re-genre-ing an adopted motif changes what it will match later.

ship_audit.gate: The card IS the audit — this is a cross-tenancy copy against a quota.
ship_audit.absent_case: OWED — a motif_id that is neither public nor the caller's must be refused.
ship_audit.tenancy: OWED — 🔴 THIS TOOL CROSSES THE BOUNDARY BY DESIGN, so the check is the inverse of every other one in this batch: adopting a PUBLIC motif must be allowed, and adopting another USER's private motif must not.

scenarios._original_prompt: Adopt motif — copy one of the built-in tropes into my library so I can customise it.
scenarios._why_this_prompt:
🔴 THE OLD PROMPT WAS UNANSWERABLE AND THE MODEL WAS RIGHT. It read 'copy ONE OF the built-in tropes', naming no target against 84 system motifs, and the model answered 'tell me WHICH specific motif' on every run — correct, because guessing on a write is worse than asking, and a bare 'yes' cannot answer a which-one question (measured: an explicit follow-up confirmation left it at 0/5).

This names a real system motif — cultivation.face_slap / 'Face-Slap Reversal' — and keeps the declared synonym 'adopt motif' CONTIGUOUS, which the answerability matcher requires. The tool takes a motif_id (UUID), so the chain composition_motif_search -> composition_motif_adopt is the thing under test.

A NEW QUESTION, labelled: it does not inherit the old row's conclusion and does not overwrite it.
